results.notes: Between-writer randomized comparison; round=all. No paired or first-round contrast applies. Exclusions were independently rebuilt from raw CSVs: 500 writer records, 169 exited before consent, 22 consent dropouts, 13 other non-completers, and 3 Human-only completers admitting AI use; 293 retained writers match creators.dta exactly by writer ID, story ID, and assignment. Observed writer counts are Human-only=95, one idea=100, five ideas=98; optional non-users in the AI arms are retained. Printed counts refer to PDF pp. 2, 7 and 8; n_units is the full three-arm count, not the pairwise count. Outcome variable: eval_novel_index. Reproduction checks use the paper's rating-level, three-arm OLS with an intercept and two assignment indicators, clustering by evaluator (CR1 correction and t inference with 599 df); means, coefficients, p-values and percentages are compared to PDF p. 3 at their printed precision. Completed evaluators supply 3600 ratings; dropping the 81 ratings of ineligible stories leaves 3519 ratings by 600 evaluators. All 12 relevant raw rating variables match evaluators_stories.dta exactly; no rating is missing. Arm rating counts are 1150, 1187, and 1182. Novelty is the mean of novel/original/rare; usefulness is the mean of appropriate/feasible/publishable, rederived in float64 (posted indices have only float32 rounding differences, maximum 3.18e-7). After successful reproduction, ratings are averaged within writer before means, sample SDs (ddof=1), and a two-arm participant-level OLS with HC2 are computed. Unequal numbers of ratings mean these equal-writer effects need not equal the paper's rating-weighted coefficients. All final differences are treatment minus control in the original outcome units, with no sign reversal. HC2 SE is also checked against sqrt(s_treatment^2/n_treatment + s_control^2/n_control). No classes, teams, or sessions were randomized, so n_clusters is null. Author programs were consulted as text only. The .py and .json files for analyst A were not read.

Between-writer randomized comparison; round=all. No paired or first-round contrast applies. Exclusions were independently rebuilt from raw CSVs: 500 writer records, 169 exited before consent, 22 consent dropouts, 13 other non-completers, and 3 Human-only completers admitting AI use; 293 retained writers match creators.dta exactly by writer ID, story ID, and assignment. Printed counts refer to PDF pp. 2, 7 and 8; n_units is the full three-arm count, not the pairwise count. Outcome is the deposited sim_idea score (cosine similarity multiplied by 100), one value per writer, including the deposited assigned comparison idea for non-users. This anchoring outcome is with_ai/other, not set-level diversity. The printed coefficient, Human-only mean, percentage and p-value on PDF p. 5 are reproduced using three-arm OLS, HC1 covariance and t inference with 290 df, matching the authors' Stata vce(robust) specification. The requested final two-arm uncertainty is HC2. Authors' code, read only as text, names text-embedding-ada-002 and assigns non-users an idea within topic (consistent with PDF p. 5; p. 8 instead says condition). No API was called, no idea resampled, and no embeddings regenerated: these statistics analyze the published per-writer scores. Two posted Stata story strings have encoding artifacts relative to raw CSV; neither texts nor published scores were altered. All final differences are treatment minus control in the original outcome units, with no sign reversal. HC2 SE is also checked against sqrt(s_treatment^2/n_treatment + s_control^2/n_control). No classes, teams, or sessions were randomized, so n_clusters is null. Author programs were consulted as text only. The .py and .json files for analyst A were not read.
